relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with "Neonatal Alexander disease." and "a GFAP pathogenic germline variant (c.716G>T p.(Arg239Leu))", plus his mother tested for the variant.
method_note: Hand-built from a short case report (no tables); a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and checked spans verbatim. In scope: the single patient (label 'patient'; 'Our patient' is a role word) and his asymptomatic mother, who was tested and found to have 'maternal somatic mosaicism for this variant' (variant row with zygosity mosaic; variant string taken from the proband's sentence that 'this variant' refers to). Patient inheritance recorded as 'inherited maternal' under D-24 because the paper states the mother carries the same variant (as somatic mosaicism); the paper never says 'inherited', and father was not reported as tested. Zygosity of the patient not stated, so 'not reported'; variant type not stated. Age at onset taken as 'a few weeks of age' (concern about delayed development) rather than presentation at 2 months with seizure; antenatal polyhydramnios also reported. Age at death and age at genetic diagnosis not stated (genetic testing result available post-mortem). 'Without accompanying foetal abnormalities' (antenatal) not recorded as an excluded feature because hypertelorism and micrognathia were noted after birth. 'Asymptomatic' for the mother not recorded as an excluded feature (a global statement). Many findings are autopsy/histopathology rather than clinical or MRI; recorded as observed features with 'at autopsy' detail. Checklist: 'recurrent vomiting' left not reported (vomiting stated, recurrence not); 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' left not reported (generalised hypertonia only); 'medulla or cervical spinal cord atrophy or signal abnormality' left not reported (brain stem atrophic at autopsy and Rosenthal fibres in medulla, but no medulla-specific atrophy/signal statement; 'no intramedullary lesions' refers to the spinal cord and does not exclude the composite item); 'basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality' observed from autopsy findings, not MRI; 'eye movement abnormality' observed from absent oculocephalic reflexes. Biopsy initially treated as low-grade glioma (vincristine and carboplatin). No contradictions found.
